comment: The same pattern a third time, in the supply chain. The Product and Supplier Registries are DPI-H components, but "the operational systems that run the supply chain — forecasting, order, warehouse, procurement, transport, and dispensing applications" sit outside DPI-H. Yet a requisition runs a lifecycle across supplier → warehouse → facility (order → dispatch → transport → receipt), and nothing tracks it to completion or flags a stall. This shows the draft's boundary choice — shared registries as DPI-H, dynamic multi-party exchange as application-layer — recurring across clinical care, financing, and supply chain. We recommend recognising the shared exchange fabric (C1, C2) as applying to all three, rather than treating exchange as an application concern in each domain separately.

This shows the draft's boundary choice — shared registries as DPI-H, dynamic multi-party exchange as application-layer — recurring across clinical care, financing, and supply chain.
